meta.description: AIRA deterministic triage and safety rules (Schema v2).

rules.condition: Airway obstruction, epiglottitis, deep neck infection, or peritonsillar abscess

paani bhi nahi nigal pa raha

hi: पानी भी नहीं निगल पा रहा

rules.response: Inability to swallow saliva, stridor (noisy high-pitched breathing), muffled voice, or a grey throat membrane indicate dangerous airway infections like epiglottitis or peritonsillar abscess. Go to a hospital emergency room immediately.
This sounds like a severe allergic reaction (angioedema or anaphylaxis) affecting the airway. Call 112 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately.

rules.condition: Choking and acute foreign body airway obstruction
rules.response: Choking is a life-threatening airway emergency. Perform back blows or the Heimlich maneuver and call 112 immediately.

rules.condition: Severe asthma exacerbation / acute respiratory distress

en: too short of breath to talk

rules.response: Severe asthma attacks not relieved by inhalers or accompanied by chest indrawing are life-threatening. Call 112 or go to an emergency room immediately.
Severe difficulty breathing, gasping, or bluish lips indicate respiratory distress. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.
Severe chest pain, chest tightness, or pain spreading to the arm or jaw are warning signs of a heart attack. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital emergency department immediately.

Sudden weakness on one side of the face or body, difficulty speaking, or sudden loss of vision are signs of a stroke. Time is critical. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital with stroke facilities immediately.

rules.response: Spreading redness, black discoloration (gangrene), foul odor, or high fever in a person with a diabetic foot ulcer indicates severe tissue infection or sepsis. Go to a hospital immediately.

rules.condition: Bacterial skin infection with sepsis or necrosis
rules.response: Severe skin infections with rapidly spreading discoloration, dead tissue, or signs of sepsis are dangerous emergencies. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.

rules.response: Fever or chills with flank/kidney pain or urinary symptoms indicates a serious upper kidney infection (pyelonephritis) or sepsis. Go to a hospital emergency department immediately.

rules.response: Sinus or facial symptoms accompanied by eye bulging, vision changes, stiff neck, or dark tissue discharge indicate severe complications. Go to a hospital emergency department immediately.

rules.condition: Severe dehydration and shock in acute diarrhoea

rules.response: Signs of severe dehydration (sunken eyes, skin pinch taking >2 seconds, inability to drink) can rapidly lead to shock. Go to a hospital or primary health centre immediately for IV fluids.

rules.condition: Dengue warning signs and severe dengue / dengue shock
rules.response: Persistent vomiting, severe stomach pain, bleeding gums, or cold clammy skin in dengue are critical warning signs of severe dengue or shock. Go to a hospital immediately.
Severe low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) causing unconsciousness or inability to swallow is a medical emergency. Call 112 or go to the nearest emergency room immediately.

A nosebleed that does not stop after 20 minutes of firm continuous pressure, causes heavy bleeding, follows facial trauma, or causes dizziness requires emergency care. Go to the nearest emergency room or hospital.

hi_latn: pregnant hai aur khoon beh raha hai

rules.response: Vaginal bleeding during pregnancy requires immediate emergency obstetric assessment. Go to the nearest maternity hospital or call 112 or 102 immediately.

phrases: बहुत ज्यादा खून बह रहा है
bohot zyada khoon beh raha hai

hi: बहुत ज्यादा खून बह रहा है
hi_latn: bohot zyada khoon beh raha hai

rules.response: Severe or uncontrolled bleeding is a medical emergency. Apply firm, continuous pressure with a clean cloth and call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.

rules.condition: Vomiting blood, black or tarry stools
rules.response: Vomiting blood or passing black, tarry stools indicates internal bleeding. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.
Seizures or convulsions require immediate medical evaluation. Ensure the person is in a safe space on their side and call 112 or go to the nearest hospital.
Loss of consciousness or unresponsiveness is a critical emergency. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately.

rules.condition: Poisoning, overdose, swallowed pesticide or chemicals
rules.response: Poisoning or chemical ingestion is a life-threatening emergency. Call 112 or go to the nearest hospital immediately with the container of the substance.
A snake bite requires immediate emergency treatment with anti-venom. Keep the bitten limb still, do not cut or suck the bite, and go to the nearest hospital immediately. Call 112.

rules.response: Head injury accompanied by vomiting, drowsiness, or confusion may indicate bleeding in the brain. Go to the nearest hospital or call 112 immediately.

rules.response: If you are feeling overwhelmed or having thoughts of self-harm, support is available right now. Please call the national mental health helpline Tele-MANAS at 14416 (toll-free, 24/7) or call 112. You do not have to go through this alone.
AIRA cannot give medication doses or drug prescription instructions. Please consult a doctor or pharmacist for safe, personalized medication advice.
AIRA provides guideline information only and cannot diagnose medical conditions. Please see a qualified healthcare professional for a clinical examination and diagnosis.

AIRA cannot change its rules. Describe your symptoms and AIRA will tell you what the guidelines say.
AIRA version 1 covers adults. For a child who is unwell, see a doctor or health worker today. In an emergency call 112.

rules.condition: Sudden severe thunderclap headache or subarachnoid hemorrhage
rules.response: A sudden, extremely severe headache reaching peak intensity within seconds (thunderclap headache) can indicate bleeding in the brain. Go to a hospital emergency room immediately.
Extensive fungal skin infection covering large areas of the body requires a medical consultation for oral antifungal prescription.
Fungal infection with no improvement after four weeks of regular treatment requires medical assessment.
Fungal skin infection that keeps returning repeatedly requires a medical evaluation to confirm diagnosis and resistance.
Prolonged use of steroid creams on a fungal rash can worsen the infection and requires medical review.
Eczema with pus discharge, yellow crusts, or increasing warmth indicates a bacterial infection requiring medical treatment.
Widespread skin blistering or skin breakdown in eczema requires medical evaluation.
Eczema associated with fever requires prompt medical examination to rule out systemic infection.
Severe eczema covering large parts of the body not responding to primary care treatment requires a doctor consultation.
Thick, yellow-brown crusts on the skin suggest crusted scabies and require specialized clinical management.
Scabies skin that is red, warm, and leaking pus indicates a secondary bacterial infection requiring antibiotics.
Spreading skin redness or sores not responding to treatment require medical examination.
Persistent itchy nodules over the genital area require doctor evaluation for nodular scabies.
